The webpage content provided does **not include specific dollar amounts** for pricing tiers. Here's what is available:

The page states plans include "monthly credits" but actual pricing figures are absent from this content. It notes: "Plans are priced by the credits they include, not by seats."

- **Plan Mode:** 1 credit per message
- **Expiration:** Monthly credits expire 2 months after issue; annual credits expire 1 month after period ends; top-up credits last 12 months

- "Credits aren't refundable or redeemable for cash"

- "Workspaces support unlimited members on all plans"

# Lovable's Backend Architecture

## Native Cloud Backend

Lovable features a **built-in backend (Cloud)** that is the default option. As stated: "Lovable's built-in backend (Cloud) is enabled by default, so most projects never need a separate Supabase account."

This native offering provides database, authentication, storage, edge functions, and real-time capabilities without requiring external setup.

## Supabase Integration

Supabase is a **partner/optional integration**, not the primary backend. The documentation notes: "It utilizes Supabase's open-source foundation, so you get the same database, auth, storage, and edge function capabilities without any setup" through the built-in backend.

You can optionally connect your own Supabase project for greater control and ownership of infrastructure.

## Authentication Approach

Authentication works differently depending on your choice:
- **Built-in backend**: Configure auth directly through Lovable, including social login providers
- **Own Supabase project**: Configure authentication settings in the Supabase dashboard instead

The documentation states that "configuring auth through Lovable" including social logins "works on the built-in backend only."

## Summary

Lovable operates a first-party cloud backend by default, with Supabase as an optional alternative for teams preferring to own their infrastructure.

# Bolt Authentication Overview

Based on the documentation, Bolt provides **built-in, first-party authentication** for generated apps through its Bolt Database.

## Supported Providers

Bolt natively supports:

1. **Email Authentication** - Users can "sign up using their email address" with customizable settings for confirmation requirements and password security.

2. **Google SSO** - The platform enables "sign up using Google Single Sign-On (SSO), meaning they can log in with their Google accounts instead of signing up with an email and password."

## Key Features

The authentication system is tightly integrated with Bolt Database and includes:

- **Leaked password protection** powered by HaveIBeenPwned (enabled by default)
- Customizable email templates with dynamic variables
- Advanced options for Site URL and URI allow lists
- Built-in password reset functionality

The documentation notes that "Bolt Database email templates are powered by Supabase technology," indicating the underlying infrastructure, but the auth implementation itself is presented as Bolt's own offering.

# Tokens at Bolt: Overview

## What Are Tokens?
"Tokens are small pieces of text. Short, common words like 'I', 'love', and 'cats' are typically one token each, but longer or less common words can be split into several." They represent the fundamental unit AI uses to process language in Bolt.

## Metering & Consumption
Bolt consumes tokens when processing your project—reading files, generating responses, and building code. Usage is "calculated based on how many tokens get processed," with larger projects using more per message. Tokens are consumed oldest-first, meaning rollover tokens from previous cycles deplete before current-period allocations.

## Free Tier Limits
- **Daily limit:** 300K tokens
- **Monthly reset:** 1st of each calendar month
- **No rollover:** Unused tokens don't carry forward; free plan tokens exist as fixed monthly buckets

## Paid Plan Limits & Reset
Renewal dates align with subscription start dates (e.g., subscribed July 15 = resets monthly on the 15th).

## Rollover Rules
Paid subscribers retain unused tokens for two months from their original issue date. Upon renewal, you receive a new allocation valid for two months. Rollover tokens are consumed first. If you cancel mid-cycle after exceeding 1 million tokens used, you must wait until the next month to access free tier tokens again.

## Extra Token Costs
Upgrading to higher-tier plans is "the most cost-effective option." Alternatively, Pro subscribers can purchase token reloads (non-expiring). Annual plans offer lower per-token pricing on higher-tier plans than lower-tier ones.

Research complete. Here are the verified findings.

---

# 1. LOVABLE (lovable.dev)

**Backend / database — FIRST-PARTY, built on Supabase's open-source foundation**
- Lovable Cloud is the default built-in backend: database, storage, auth, realtime, functions. "Lovable's built-in backend (Cloud) is enabled by default, so most projects never need a separate Supabase account." — https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/supabase
- It "utilizes Supabase's open-source foundation," so it is first-party-branded but Supabase-derived under the hood. — https://docs.lovable.dev/features/cloud
- Connecting your own Supabase project remains available as an optional path for infra ownership. — https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/supabase

**Auth**
- Configured directly through Lovable, including social login providers; docs state configuring auth through Lovable "works on the built-in backend only." If you bring your own Supabase project, you configure auth in the Supabase dashboard instead. — https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/supabase
- Cloud includes user authentication with sign-in methods such as Google OAuth. — https://docs.lovable.dev/features/cloud

**Server vs client-only / hosting**
- Real server-side backend, not client-only. Apps are hosted on Lovable's servers in one of three regions (Americas, Europe, Asia Pacific), chosen at Cloud setup and **not changeable afterward**. — https://docs.lovable.dev/features/cloud
- Lovable manages both frontend and backend on its own infrastructure, with custom domains, automatic SSL, and global delivery. Code is exportable via Git sync; you can self-host part or all of the stack. — https://docs.lovable.dev/tips-tricks/deployment-hosting-ownership
- Generated apps are "standard Vite + React projects" (client-rendered frontend + backend services). — https://docs.lovable.dev/tips-tricks/deployment-hosting-ownership
- *Unverified:* the specific claim that every publish deploys as an edge Worker with pre-rendered routes came from a third-party blog, not Lovable docs.

**Templates / starters — YES, explicitly**
- "Design templates": Design → Use a template. "A design template is a Lovable project that has been marked as reusable," and using one **copies the entire project codebase into the new project**. — https://docs.lovable.dev/features/business/design-templates
- Public template gallery at https://lovable.dev/templates (websites, portfolios, etc.)
- *Note:* I found no official Lovable statement framing templates as a **cost/credit-reduction** mechanism. That framing is verified for Bolt (below), not Lovable. Treat "Lovable uses templates to reduce generation cost" as unverified.

**Pricing — metered in CREDITS**
- Free: 5 build credits/day, capped at 30/month; plus 20 Cloud credits/month and 4 AI credits/month. — https://lovable.dev/pricing and https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/subscription-plans
- Pro: **from $25/month for 100 credits**, scaling up to **$2,250/month for 10,000 credits**. — https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/subscription-plans
- Business: **from $50/month for 100 credits**, scaling to **$4,300/month for 10,000 credits**; adds SSO, restricted projects, data opt-out, design templates. — https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/subscription-plans
- Enterprise: custom contract; excludes the standard Cloud/AI grants. — https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/subscription-plans
- Annual pricing (~$21/mo Pro, ~$42/mo Business) appeared in search snippets but I could **not** confirm it on an official page — **unverified**.
- Metering unit detail: Default Mode credit cost **varies by task complexity** (examples cited: 0.50–1.70 credits per message); Plan Mode is a flat 1 credit/message. Monthly credits expire 2 months after issue; annual credits expire 1 month after the period ends; top-up credits last 12 months. Credits are non-refundable and not redeemable for cash. "Plans are priced by the credits they include, not by seats" — workspaces support unlimited members on all plans. — https://lovable.dev/pricing

**Credit-burn incidents**
- No official Lovable incident disclosure found. Complaints are third-party/anecdotal: bug-fix loops consuming credits, and users reporting no visibility into cost before a message runs. — https://dev.to/momen_hq/the-hidden-costs-of-vibe-coding-a-practical-look-at-lovables-credit-usage-3cec
- Specific figures circulating ("30 credits for one bug fix", "65–75% bug-loop rate") come from blog/marketing content with no primary source — **unverified**.

---

# 2. BOLT.NEW (StackBlitz)

**Backend / database — first-party branded "Bolt Database", powered by Supabase**
- Supabase's own launch post states plainly: "every project in Bolt Cloud that needs a backend is powered by Supabase." Published **September 30, 2025**. Includes Postgres, auth/user management (incl. SAML/SSO), S3-compatible file+video storage, Edge Functions, Realtime APIs. Notes Bolt had already connected apps to **over 600,000 Supabase backends**. — https://supabase.com/blog/bolt-cloud-launch
- Bolt's own docs present it as first-party: "Create and manage databases in Bolt without the need for third-party tools," with unlimited databases, built-in auth management, file storage, server functions. Connecting your own Supabase project is offered as an **alternative** ("Use Supabase instead of Bolt database"). Unpublished projects auto-pause after ~6+ days of low usage. — https://support.bolt.new/cloud/database
- Bolt Cloud also involves a Netlify partnership for hosting per third-party reporting — **partially unverified** (Netlify is confirmed as an optional publish target in Bolt's own docs: https://support.bolt.new/integrations/netlify).

**Auth — built-in, Supabase-backed**
- Native email/password signup and **Google SSO**. Leaked-password protection via HaveIBeenPwned enabled by default; customizable email templates; built-in password reset. Docs acknowledge "Bolt Database email templates are powered by Supabase technology." — https://support.bolt.new/cloud/database/authentication

**Server vs client-only / hosting**
- **Two distinct runtimes.** During *generation/preview*, the app runs client-side in StackBlitz **WebContainers** — a full Node.js runtime executing inside the browser tab (filesystem, terminal, package manager, dev server all client-side). — https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new
- When *published*, apps use Bolt's built-in hosting by default, with Netlify as an optional alternative target. Backend logic runs as real server/edge functions on the Supabase-powered Bolt Cloud. — https://support.bolt.new/cloud/hosting and https://support.bolt.new/integrations/netlify

**Templates / starters — YES, and explicitly framed as a token-saving mechanism**
- This is the strongest public statement of the three. Bolt's blog recommends templates "to save tokens." — https://bolt.new/blog/top-5-bolt-new-templates-to-jumpstart-your-next-project
- Official token-efficiency doc: Bolt processes fewer tokens with less context; recommends cleaning unused files, splitting large files, and using Discuss Mode to plan before building. — https://support.bolt.new/best-practices/maximizing-token-efficiency
- Reported behavior that you can build on a template **without consuming tokens until you make changes** came from third-party coverage — **unverified** against Bolt docs.

**Pricing — metered in TOKENS (LLM tokens, not credits)**
From https://bolt.new/pricing:
- Free: **$0** — 300,000 tokens/day, 1,000,000 tokens/month, 10MB file uploads, up to ~333k web requests. No rollover.
- Pro: **$25/month** — starting at 10,000,000 tokens/month, **no daily limit**, tokens roll over, 100MB uploads, up to 1M web requests.
- Teams: **$30/month per member** — same token allowances as Pro plus workspace collaboration.
- Enterprise: custom pricing and custom token allowances.

Token mechanics (https://support.bolt.new/account-and-subscription/tokens):
- Critical cost driver, in Bolt's own words: "most token usage is related to syncing your project's file system to the AI: the larger the project, the more tokens used per message." Cost scales with **codebase size**, not interaction count.
- Free tokens reset the 1st of each calendar month, no rollover. Paid tokens are retained for **two months** from issue; rollover tokens are consumed **oldest-first**.
- Pro subscribers can buy non-expiring "token reloads." Exact reload dollar prices — **unverified**.

Hosting limits (https://support.bolt.new/cloud/hosting/plans):
- Free hosting: up to 10 GB bandwidth + 333,333 requests/month, hard traffic ceiling (~10,000–15,000 monthly visits).
- Pro hosting: up to 30 GB bandwidth + 1M requests/month, with pay-as-you-go overage. Pro hosting is included with every paid Bolt subscription. **No separate dollar price is published for hosting tiers.**

**Token-burn incidents**
- A Hacker News "Ask HN" post reports a user losing 10M tokens with an unresolved support response: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46321594 — this is a **single user account, not a confirmed platform incident**. No official StackBlitz incident disclosure found. Bolt's refund policy being discretionary is reported third-party — **unverified**.

---

# 3. REPLIT / REPLIT AGENT

**Backend / database — first-party, migrated OFF Neon**
- Important and easy to get wrong: Replit Database is now "a fully-managed SQL database" that is Replit's own managed solution. The docs note that **prior to December 4, 2025**, the development database "was hosted on Neon and has a few crucial differences." So the widely-repeated "Replit is powered by Neon" claim is **outdated** for current production. — https://docs.replit.com/cloud-services/storage-and-databases/sql-database
- Includes **20GB of free storage for every Replit App**; every Replit app comes with a database by default. — same URL
- Agent provisions schema and wires an ORM automatically when asked to add a database. — https://docs.replit.com/cloud-services/storage-and-databases/sql-database

**Auth — first-party "Replit Auth"**
- Agent-only: "Manual implementation is not supported, as Agent handles all the complexity for you." Triggered by saying "use Replit Auth" in a prompt. — https://docs.replit.com/replit-workspace/replit-auth
- End users sign in with existing Replit accounts; login methods include Google, GitHub, X, Apple, and Email. Underlying vendors named in docs: Firebase, Google Cloud, reCAPTCHA, Stytch, Clearout. — same URL
- Auth pane provides user management; auto-creates user entries in your database.

**Server vs client-only / hosting — real servers, priced separately from Agent**
Replit is the clearest "real server" of the three, and notably **hosting is billed separately from Agent usage** (https://docs.replit.com/billing/deployment-pricing):
- Autoscale (default/recommended): **$2.00/month base + $0.60 per million compute units + $0.40 per million requests**; scales to zero when idle.
- Reserved VM: **$15.00/mo** (shared 0.5 vCPU / 2GB), **$35.00** (dedicated 1 vCPU / 4GB), **$50.00** (2 vCPU / 8GB), **$130.00** (4 vCPU / 16GB).
- Scheduled: $2.00/month + $0.60/M compute units; scheduler free.
- Static: hosting free, **$0.05/GB** data transfer.
- Replit's own cost examples: small business site (~75k monthly requests) ≈ $2.39/mo; API service (300k requests) ≈ $4.50/mo.

**Templates / starters — YES**
- Custom Templates: Enterprise admins create pre-configured starting points that appear directly in the Agent input box. "When a builder selects a custom template, Agent forks it and uses the template's configuration, instructions, and skills to guide all subsequent work." — https://docs.replit.com/teams/custom-templates
- Public gallery: https://replit.com/gallery
- No official statement framing templates as a **cost-reduction** measure — **unverified**.

**Pricing — metered in "effort-based" CHECKPOINTS/credits**
From https://replit.com/pricing:
- Starter (Free): $0, free daily usage, create projects and publish **1 live project**, built-in database access.
- Core: **$25/mo, or $20/mo billed annually**; includes **$25 toward most powerful models**, 2 parallel agents, unlimited workspaces, badge removal.
- Pro: **$100/mo, or $95/mo billed annually**; includes **$100 toward most powerful models**, 10 parallel agents, up to 15 collaborators + 50 viewers, 28-day database rollback, premium support.
- Enterprise: custom; SSO/SAML, single-tenant, static outbound IPs.
- The official pricing page does **not** publish specific credit counts for free daily usage — **unverified**.

Effort-based pricing mechanics (https://replit.com/blog/effort-based-pricing, published **June 18, 2025**, updated July 2, 2025):
- Old model: flat **$0.25 per checkpoint**. Small edits cost $0.25; large tasks fragmented into multiple $0.25 checkpoints.
- New model charges by "effort" measured in **time and computation**. Simple changes cost **less than $0.25**; complex tasks bundle into one checkpoint that "may cost more than $0.25." "Cost will reflect the true scope of the Agent's work."
- Two user-facing effort dials: "High power model" and "Extended thinking."
- Rollout: immediate for new users, from **July 1, 2025** for existing Core and Teams subscribers. (Note: some third-party pages misdate this as 2026 — the primary source is 2025.)
- Third-party figures like "simple edits 5–20 credits, complex features 150–300+ credits" are **unverified** against Replit docs.

**Surprise-bill incidents — THIS IS THE BEST-DOCUMENTED CASE OF THE THREE, with official admission**
Replit publicly acknowledged the problem (https://replit.com/blog/effort-based-pricing-recap):
- Replit stated "the transition to the new pricing model did not meet our standards for how we like to roll out major changes."
- **July 11 billing incident**: between 11:26 AM and 5:43 PM PDT, "checkpoint charges were being incorrectly computed and were often much larger than they should have been," affecting **~6% of paying users**. Automatic refunds/credits were issued for the full cost of affected checkpoints, no user action required.
- Replit gave **$10 in free credits to all members** who used the new pricing model.

Subsequent Agent 3 backlash (mid-September 2025), per https://www.infoworld.com/article/4059876/replit-update-sparks-developers-dissatisfaction-over-pricing.html:
- Users reported consuming "a third of their monthly budget in one night." Root cause cited: Agent 3's increased autonomy triggering unnecessary refactoring on minor edits.
- CEO Amjad Masad acknowledged the Agent 3 issues and said the company was "actively trying to fix them." InfoWorld did **not** publish specific dollar amounts.
- Larger figures circulating in search summaries (one user charged $1K in a week; another $1,982 in 24 days; another ~$700/month) trace to a Register article at https://www.theregister.com/software/2025/09/18/replit-infuriating-customers-with-surprise-cost-overruns/ which **returned HTTP 404 on direct fetch** — I could not verify these numbers against the primary source. Treat as **unverified**.
- A Trustpilot reviewer reported ~$500/week and being charged for agent idle/freeze time — single anecdote, **unverified**: https://www.trustpilot.com/review/replit.com

---

# CROSS-CUTTING NOTES

**The three metering units are genuinely different, which makes direct comparison misleading:**
- Lovable = **credits** (variable per message, 0.50–1.70 typical in Default Mode)
- Bolt = **LLM tokens** (scales with codebase size, since the filesystem is re-synced to the AI each message)
- Replit = **effort-based checkpoints** (time + computation, price revealed *after* the checkpoint is charged)

**All three are Supabase-adjacent except Replit.** Lovable Cloud and Bolt Database are both Supabase-powered but first-party-branded. Replit is the only one running its own database stack (and moved off Neon in December 2025).

**Only Bolt has an official public statement tying templates to cost reduction** ("save tokens"). Lovable and Replit both ship templates that fork/copy an entire project codebase, but neither publicly frames this as a generation-cost lever.

**Hidden-cost asymmetry:** Replit bills app hosting separately from Agent credits (Autoscale/Reserved VM line items), while Lovable and Bolt bundle hosting into the plan with bandwidth/request caps. A Replit user's true monthly cost is plan + agent effort + deployment.

**Verification gaps, stated plainly:** Lovable annual pricing; Lovable's edge-Worker deploy architecture; Bolt token reload prices; Bolt Pro hosting dollar price; Replit free-tier credit counts; all specific user-reported dollar figures in the Replit and Bolt billing controversies (The Register article 404'd on direct fetch).
